drafted_from: tools/pointillist-film/tool-rows.json (tool:render-pointillist-frames-over-time), examples/encode_frame_sequence.rs, test/pointillist-film.test.mjs; the example was run here with cargo
start_here: Say to your AI: "Render my two-cell film at 0, 1 and 1.5 seconds into a folder of frames." It runs encode_frame_sequence on your computer and tells you where the three frame files are.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one sequence file and writes numbered frame files into a folder.
instructions: 1. Install rust (cargo) and clone the Workshop repository. The first run builds the program (about a minute; a few seconds once built).
2. Write sequence.json: {request: <the single-frame request, its time_seconds is replaced>, times_seconds: [0, 1, 1.5]}.

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:render-pointillist-frames-over-time"} and runs: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/pointillist-film/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/pointillist-film-build --example encode_frame_sequence -- sequence.json frames

4. Read the folder: frame-0000.pfcf, frame-0001.pfcf and so on, one for each time in the order given, each the same packed frame the single-frame tool writes for that time. A request that breaks a limit prints the reason and exits non-zero.

worked_examples.title: Three frames of a two-cell film
worked_examples.ask: Render my two-cell film at 0, 1 and 1.5 seconds.
worked_examples.given: From tools/pointillist-film/test/pointillist-film.test.mjs (the sequence test) and run here with cargo: sequence.json holds the request for a two-cell film (grid 2 columns by 1 row, gap 0.1; limits max 8 columns, 8 rows, 64 cells, 4 targets, 4096 frame bytes; style opacity 0 to 1, scale 0 to 4; target 0 is a red cell and a blue cell, target 1 is a green cell and a yellow cell; one segment from 0 s for 2 s that weights target 0 by the constant 1 and target 1 by the input time) and times_seconds [0, 1, 1.5]. The AI runs: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/pointillist-film/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/pointillist-film-build --example encode_frame_sequence -- sequence.json frames
worked_examples.hands_back: Nothing on standard output and exit 0; the folder frames holds frame-0000.pfcf, frame-0001.pfcf and frame-0002.pfcf, each 54 bytes and beginning PFCF; the first (time 0) and the last (time 1.5) differ in their bytes because target 1 weighs more as time passes.
